# Retrospective: PR 12844 follow-up

## Worked

Fresh exact-model sessions, equivalent neutral assignments, public-only history and both-finals-before-reading preserved independent technical reasoning. Reviewer disagreement concerned public relevance rather than an unresolved source trace. The narrow public scope avoids a blanket assertion about all Git-error repair paths. Explicit source-only publication is preferable to retaining nonconforming runtime totals.

## Deviations and correction

1. Coordinator initially read README/workflow in calls exceeding the newer 60-line policy-read bound, before reaching that correction. The complete tail was subsequently read before lifecycle control/runtime work; native history retained. Later policy reads were bounded. Current assignment instructions already tell reviewers to start with bounded complete reads. No technical claim relies on truncated policy output.
2. Opus intentionally wrote an output-inventory analysis to the native scratchpad outside the assignment, then moved it into evidence/misplaced with its hash. Native history and the incident record are retained. This is a storage deviation, not evidence that private data was sent upstream. Assignment-local paths must be supplied for every analysis redirect, not just test output.
3. The initial fixture/report overclaimed per-final-target guards. Coordinator read the complete driver/stubs and identified unguarded transitive mkdir/venv/marker/append/clone targets. Opus confirmed and withdrew those claims in audit-addendum.md. All broad runtime totals and runtime reliance were excluded from synthesis/publication; pinned source-supported claims remain. No corrected runtime rerun was needed for the source-only conclusions. Post-hoc containment and a seal do not establish prior compliance.
4. A pre-pin regex edit damaged a fixture stub, was inspected and repaired before any execution. The pre-edit draft remains, but the damaged intermediate was not preserved. One rejected Edit had no effect. Neither is behavioral evidence.

See PROCESS-CORRECTIONS.md for the assignment-local correction forwarded in this round. Do not call the process fully compliant. No known isolation escape, independence contamination or quota exhaustion occurred. No further technical blocker remains for the source-scoped comment.

## Limits and resources

Real package/upstream installation, real mise at current head, self-update, authentication and desktop operation were not validated. No desktop slot was used. Foreground sandbox runs ended with their namespaces; no owned background processes or services remain. Reviewer panes and immutable source/evidence remain intentionally. No browser opened and no upstream write performed.

## Improvement

Before pinning, compare a literal final-target checklist to each stub/helper body. Include native Git mutation roots, parent mkdir, helper log appends, backup/staging and cache paths. Never infer individual guards from a parent root, summary total or successful seal. Prefer source-only assessment when source settles the material question and a compliant runtime fixture adds little. No confirmed review.py/Herdr/Omadev product bug was established.
comment:
**Verified by source inspection:** At `73a2b91c`, the [app-only installation change](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12844#issuecomment-5788917626) is reflected in both installer modes. No new substantive issue was identified in these changed paths.

| Condition | Current handling |
|---|---|
| Working Hermes without the desktop package | `--check` rejects it; `--now` takes the app installation path rather than standing aside. |
| Ready runtime, no seeded app, newer than the packaged release | Refuses with build-only guidance before backing up or replacing existing commands. |
| Ready runtime, no seeded app, unreadable HEAD or desktop-source status | Explicitly checks the Git failure and refuses before command replacement. |

The refusal checks above concern a **ready runtime without a seeded app**, not every repair path. Eligible installations still save existing commands before replacement. Choosing the default agent uses the shared setup without opening the desktop window.

The [previously resolved mise-shadowing finding](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12844#issuecomment-5775266701) remains resolved in the inspected source: ownership-gated retirement and the final PATH check remain in place. This does not repeat the earlier real-mise reproduction or establish whole-PR correctness.
